title: Minor NSR permits: the air permit that decides when a data center can power itself
map_limitation: Five blind spots specific to THIS map. (1) THE LOAD-BEARING WEAKNESS, carried from the signal rather than discovered late: no source fetched this run attributes a single dollar of generator, turbine, catalyst or fuel demand to the EPA minor-NSR public-participation rule specifically. The demand is real and dated (Caterpillar power generation retail sales up 72% year over year, GE Vernova data center orders above $5 billion year to date, a data center generator market put at USD 10.34 billion in 2026), and it is being bought for grid-queue reasons that would exist if this rulemaking had never been signed. Every link here is scored on the MECHANISM, that minor NSR is the permit class gating on-site generation, and never on an attribution nobody has published. A heat run that reads this map as a measure of the rule's marginal contribution is reading it wrong. (2) The two links that own the schedule publish nothing and cannot be bought. federal-minor-nsr-rule is a docket and state-air-permitting-authority is fifty-odd state and local bureaus, so both carry zero tickers by design, and the only quantity anyone has measured against data centers at all is a Georgia count of 20 permits since January 2025 against 17 in 2014 to 2024, which is one state, from one public broadcaster, via an SIC search. (3) Supplier-side EDGAR full-text search is close to useless on the two stages that matter most here, because the work is bought as professional services and as private packaging. Trinity Consultants, ERM, Ramboll and SLR do the air permitting; Cormetech (now inside Johnson Matthey), Miratech, DCL International and EcoCAT do the aftertreatment; VoltaGrid, ProEnergy, Crusoe, Mainspring and Enchanted Rock own the plants; Mansfield Energy, Sun Coast Resources, Foster Fuels and Ricochet Fuel move the diesel; Kohler and Eurodiesel Services build gensets; Aggreko and APR Energy rent them. None of them files with the SEC. The listed names that do this work largely file elsewhere: WSP.TO, STN.TO, ARCAD.AS, AFRY.ST, JMAT.L, ATCO-A.ST, ABBN.SW, WRT1V.HE, AHT.L, ENGI.PA, ENR.DE, SU.PA and HPS-A.TO all reach this map through research, not through fts. (4) BLK-04, declared twice on this map rather than once. power-equipment-shared at position 10 IS ai-infrastructure/power-equipment, carried with a byte-identical ticker list so the duplication is visible, and it is now the THIRD chain to touch that one stage after ai-infrastructure (the owner) and data-center-moratoria (declared). Separately, eight of the nine tickers at air-permitting-and-dispersion-modeling also sit on data-center-moratoria/permitting-and-environmental-consultancy: different practice group, same issuer, one bet. ONT is the only name there that is not on the moratoria list. Non-US ticker share is 15 of 51, and that is a property of a US federal permitting occurrence rather than an omission: positions 1, 2, 8, 9, 13 and 14 are US agencies, US pipelines, US fuel haulage and US campuses, and putting a foreign name on any of them would be invention. (5) Three claims on this map are directionally sourced and quantitatively soft. The edge from state-air-permitting-authority to bridge-power-rental-fleets rests on EPA tightening interpretations of how long mobile turbines may run unpermitted, which is a mechanism and not a measured rental dollar. The fuel-cell route-around at position 7 is evidenced as a permitting and speed claim (near-zero NOx, often exempt, 100 MW in as little as 90 days) and NOT as a margin or share claim, so it caps the rest of the map qualitatively. And no fetched source isolates a data-center air-permitting or emissions-monitoring margin at any listed consultancy, so capture at positions 3 and 11 cannot be read off any market-size number.

notes.text: SHARED-STAGE DECLARATION, campaign blocker BLK-04, and this map makes TWO of them. First: power-equipment-shared at position 10 IS ai-infrastructure/power-equipment. Same stage, same seven tickers, deliberately identical so the duplication is visible on the map instead of discovered in a census. No issuer on that link may be counted toward this theme's issuer coverage; they belong to ai-infrastructure/power-equipment. Heat is scored once, there, and inherited here. This is the third chain to touch that stage, after ai-infrastructure (owner) and data-center-moratoria (declared on 2026-08-30), and the note on that chain asked for exactly this declaration when the rank-8 theme was built. It is included rather than omitted because a permitted generation fleet cannot be energized without switchgear, and a map that stops at the engine is incomplete. Second, and not previously flagged by anyone: eight of the nine tickers at air-permitting-and-dispersion-modeling (TTEK, ACM, J, WSP.TO, STN.TO, ARCAD.AS, AFRY.ST, WLDN) also sit on data-center-moratoria/permitting-and-environmental-consultancy. That is a PARTIAL duplicate: different practice group inside the same issuer. It is declared here and in map_limitation so a universe run attributes each issuer to one theme and says which. Third, deliberately NOT built here: this chain does not carry a grid-interconnection or utility-generation link at all. That is ai-infrastructure/grid-interconnect and ai-infrastructure/energy-generation, and the whole point of this map is what happens when the campus does not wait for them.

THE THESIS WAS TESTED AND IT DID NOT SURVIVE INTACT. The signal reads minor NSR as a schedule story: remove the mandatory comment window and the fastest path to powering a campus gets faster. Tested both ways. FOR: the permit class is demonstrably the one gating on-site generation (Georgia, 20 data-center generator permits since January 2025 against 17 in the prior decade), the modeling work sits on the critical path by the practitioners' own account (air dispersion modeling requirements affect application preparation and agency review timelines and in turn the overall project schedule), and regulators are explicitly focused on potential-to-emit, NSR thresholds and operating-hour limits as on-site units move from backup to sustained runtime. AGAINST, and this is the correction: the rule hands DISCRETION to states, and discretion is not a direction. In the largest data-center state that has moved, Virginia, the discretion is being used to TIGHTEN, with a presumptive 0.60 g/hp-hr limit for large data center generators and a Tier 4 baseline applying to applications submitted on or after July 1, 2026, the same day EPA signed the federal loosening. A map that assumed one-way shortening would have been wrong on its central claim within eight weeks. So the schedule effect is recorded as state by state at position 2, not as a federal constant. SECOND CORRECTION: position 7 exists because the strongest competitor to this entire chain is a technology that deletes the permit rather than satisfying it. Fuel cells produce virtually no NOx and are often exempt from the air permits that delay combustion projects, and nearly half of planned data center sites sit in nonattainment zones. Any capture scored at positions 4, 5, 6 and 11 is competing against that.

ARCHETYPES APPLIED, and two checked for ABSENCE. ARCH-003 three times, which is the most on any chain in the corpus: federal-minor-nsr-rule and state-air-permitting-authority are the classic uninvestable order-book owners (zero tickers, they set everyone's schedule), and behind-the-meter-power-developers is the third and the commercially important one, because the order book every supplier link sells into is VoltaGrid, ProEnergy, Crusoe and Mainspring, all private. Then data-center-developer-demand INVERTS it exactly as data-center-moratoria did: the anchor is fully listed and fully crowded. ARCH-001 twice: onsite-reciprocating-gensets (Caterpillar restarting a 10-MW platform to bring back 1.5 GW) and packaged-gas-turbines (large frame units face multi-year lead times and constrained manufacturing slots). ARCH-002 twice, both in costume: air-permitting-and-dispersion-modeling is mandatory work that is competitively bid with the firm substitutable even though the study is not, and bridge-power-rental-fleets is the same shape with a fleet instead of a headcount. ARCH-004 once and translated from a material to a control device: emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst scores on substitutability (low inside a permitted engine, total across technologies via position 7) times logistics (catalyst supply just consolidated into Johnson Matthey rather than fragmenting). ARCH-005 once and declared, see the BLK-04 note. ABSENCE CHECKS: ARCH-006 (geopolitical counter-response) does NOT fire and its absence is a finding, not a gap. The counter-response to this occurrence is domestic and legal (state tightening, litigation over a Clean Air Act rulemaking), and the investable half of it already has its own map in data-center-moratoria, which is why nothing was invented here to fill the slot. ARCH-007 (semis as a leaf) does not fire either: there is no compute layer on this chain, because the occurrence gates the power plant and not the rack. No archetype was overridden and none conflicted with this chain's structure, so there is nothing for Ron to rule on.

STAGES CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, with the reason for each. (1) On-site power EPC and packaging, the integrator that parallels the gensets, builds the pad and commissions the plant. Checked and dropped: the recognised names are private (Kiewit, Burns and McDonnell, Black and Veatch, Sargent and Lundy), and the only dated release fetched this run that touches the stage (Generac with EPC Power, 2026-03-05) is about battery and inverter integration rather than about permitted generation EPC. A stage that cannot be cited is not a stage. (2) Water and wastewater permitting, which travels with air permitting on real applications. Dropped as belonging to data-center-moratoria/water-permitting-and-hydrology, where it is already built; adding it here would have been a third count of one stage in one night. (3) Grid interconnection and utility generation, dropped because it is ai-infrastructure's and because this map is specifically about not waiting for it. (4) Diesel exhaust fluid and urea supply, a real consumable created by every SCR system on this map: no dated source fetched this run connects a listed urea or DEF supplier to data-center gensets, so it is folded into the aftertreatment note rather than given a position it cannot support. (5) Noise permitting and acoustic enclosures, which the practitioner source names alongside air permitting for on-site prime power: no dated source with listed names was found, so it is not on the map.

Not CHOKE_POINT, because the rule does not itself issue or withhold a permit: it hands discretion to the fifty-odd agencies at position 2, and the discretion is two-way. scenarios.title: The rule finalises and the states use it to go faster
scenarios.narrative: EPA finalises the removal of the federal minimum public participation requirement substantially as proposed, and the large-load states take the discretion in the direction the proposal invites. Notice and comment steps come out of the minor source process in Georgia, Texas and Ohio, and permit-to-construct dates pull in by quarters rather than by weeks. The gate at position 2 widens without changing what it demands technically, so the same permit is written faster. The consequence runs down the map unevenly: the developers who file the applications get their schedule back, the equipment links convert a pipeline into shipments sooner, the consultancy loses its public participation workload while keeping its modelling workload, and the two links that live on the wait, rental bridge power and the fuel cell route around the permit, lose the reason customers pay them a premium. Note what this scenario does not claim: no source attributes a dollar of equipment demand to this rule, so what moves is TIMING, not the size of the order book.

links_moved.why: Throughput rises where the state drops the notice step. Georgia already ran 20 data center generator permits since January 2025 against 17 in the prior decade; removing a comment window compounds that run rate rather than starting it.
The application is filed in this link's name, so a shorter permit is a shorter time to revenue on projects already contracted. This is where the schedule gain is booked first and biggest.

Orders pull forward into the restarted 1.5 GW of 10-MW platform capacity. Volume is not created, it arrives earlier, which is worth more to a supplier holding constrained slots than to one with spare capacity.
Same pull-forward, on a tier where an initial award already covers approximately 1 GW to be delivered by 2030 and delivery slots are the scarce good.

More permitted units at the same SCR based control presumption means more catalyst content. The rule changes the process, not the emission limit, so content per unit is unchanged and unit count rises.
This is the only link whose demand is the delay itself. Shorten the permit and the bridge gets shorter, and the fleet that was earning for several years per site earns for fewer.
The product being sold is an exemption from a queue. Shorten the queue for combustion and the premium for avoiding it narrows, which attacks the part of the story the multiple is built on.

Two offsetting moves. Public participation support work disappears and application volume rises, and dispersion modelling is required either way, so the net is a small gain on a larger number of smaller engagements.

Permits still issue and the volume still grows, but each permit carries more control hardware, more monitoring and a heavier technical case. The schedule does not shorten and may lengthen. This is the scenario that pays the money corner on this map: the catalyst and aftertreatment link is the one stage whose content per permitted unit rises directly with the stringency of the limit, and it is scored UNDISCOVERED with the only listed name in the segment sitting at the bottom of its own 52-week range.

links_moved.why: A presumptive limit written around selective catalytic reduction leaves an engine no other way to meet it, so content per unit rises with stringency and applies to retrofit as well as new build, including Tier 2 engines fitted with add-on SCR.

The tightening template names continuous emissions monitoring alongside the control hardware, and monitoring is a life-of-plant obligation rather than a one-time sale, so it compounds with each permitted unit.

A presumptive best available control technology argument is a heavier technical case per application than a notice period, and the modelling has to defend it. Fee per engagement rises even where unit count is flat.

Every increment of combustion stringency widens the value of a technology that is often exempt from the permit entirely, particularly in the nonattainment counties where roughly half of planned sites sit.

Unit count is broadly unchanged and content per unit rises, but most of that content accrues to the aftertreatment supplier rather than to the engine maker, so the engine tier gains least of the three.
A schedule that does not shorten keeps the bridge in place, though the same tightening interpretations that limit unpermitted mobile turbine runtime cap how much of that the rental fleet can collect.
More conditions per permit means slower issuance per permit. The choke point narrows rather than widens, which is the opposite of what the federal proposal was written to do.

leading_indicators.signal: A second large-load state publishes a presumptive g/hp-hr limit or an SCR based best available control technology presumption for data center generators, following Virginia's 0.60 g/hp-hr guidance.
leading_indicators.check_basis: State guidance is a document, not a price, and position 2 carries no tickers by design.

leading_indicators.signal: Johnson Matthey clears 2600 on the LSE listing carried as data/market/JMAT-L.json, off the 2226.00 close recorded for 2026-08-27 which is the bottom of its own 2226.00 to 3184.00 fifty-two-week range, and back toward mid-range. The listed owner of the SCR catalyst business re-rating is the cleanest single price expression of a tightening template.
A listed emissions monitoring vendor names data center continuous emissions monitoring as a growth driver in a results statement or segment disclosure.
leading_indicators.check_basis: None of ONT, TDY, TMO or ABBN.SW has a file under data/market/, so no level can be set without inventing a price. Arm this after a request data run covers those tickers.

invalidation_signs: EPA finalises and the large-load states adopt the shortened notice without adding presumptive limits, leaving control content per permit flat.
Virginia softens or withdraws the 0.60 g/hp-hr presumptive limit under developer pressure, removing the template other states would copy.
New permits continue to issue with Tier 2 engines and no add-on controls at the same rate as before, which would show the presumption is not binding in practice.

scenarios.title: The rule is withdrawn or stalls and nothing downstream notices
scenarios.narrative: The comment record, the advocacy campaign and the litigation risk are enough to stop the rule. EPA withdraws it, lets it lapse without final action, or a court stays it, and the federal minimum for public notice on minor NSR permits survives intact. The important half of this scenario is what does NOT happen: the generator, turbine, catalyst and fuel order books carry on exactly as they were, because none of that demand was ever attributed by any source to this rulemaking. It is grid-queue demand that the permit authorises rather than creates. This is the map's own load-bearing weakness written as a scenario, and it is the cheapest test of the whole chain: if the rule dies and the equipment links do not move, the honest conclusion is that this chain is a mechanism worth understanding and not an occurrence worth trading.

links_moved.why: The stage is the rulemaking. A withdrawal, lapse or stay removes it, which is the maximum possible move at this position.
No discretion is gained, so the gate stays exactly as wide as it is today. Small rather than large because the status quo is already the base case in every state that has not published new guidance.
The wait does not shorten, so the bridge stays in place. Small because the demand was never sized off this rule either, and because tightening mobile runtime interpretations cut the other way.
The schedule gain they would have booked does not arrive. Small rather than medium because the projects are contracted on grid-queue economics that survive the withdrawal untouched.

leading_indicators.signal: The EPA docket shows a withdrawal notice, or the rule passes its expected final action window with no final rule published in the Federal Register.
leading_indicators.check_basis: A docket event with no instrument attached at position 1.

leading_indicators.signal: A petition for review is filed against the final rule in a federal circuit court, or a state coalition announces a challenge.
leading_indicators.check_basis: Litigation is a filing, not a price, and neither of the two links this scenario moves most carries a ticker.

leading_indicators.signal: Caterpillar holds 700 or better through the withdrawal, roughly 13 percent below the 800.25 close recorded for 2026-08-28 in data/market/CAT.json and far above the 415.12 fifty-two-week low. Holding that level while the docket dies is the observable form of the claim that no equipment demand was ever attributed to this rule.

invalidation_signs: The rule is finalised substantially as proposed, which is S1 or S2 rather than this.

Generator and turbine order intake visibly slows in the quarter a withdrawal is announced, which would mean the attribution nobody published was real after all and the whole map should be rescored on it.
State agencies begin removing notice steps on their own authority without the federal rule, which would make the docket's fate irrelevant rather than decisive.

scenarios.title: The route around wins and the permit stops being worth satisfying
scenarios.narrative: Permit avoidance beats permit satisfaction on the marginal site. Roughly half of planned data center sites sit in nonattainment counties where combustion permitting is strictest, the exempt technology claims delivery of 100 MW in as little as 90 days, and its revenue is already roughly doubling. Developers stop arguing about best available control technology and buy the machine the permit class does not gate. This is the strongest single argument against the chain's own thesis and Atlas put it on the map deliberately at position 7 for exactly this reason. Every dollar of capture scored at the aftertreatment, engine and turbine links is competing against a technology that deletes the permit rather than meeting it, and in this scenario it loses the increment regardless of what EPA finalises. The one part of the map that survives is the molecule: fuel cells still burn gas, so the root link at position 8 is indifferent to which machine burns it.

links_moved.why: The stage takes the marginal site outright. Its two selling propositions, exemption from the permit queue and 90-day delivery, are both strongest exactly where the combustion path is slowest.

No combustion permit means no best available control technology presumption and therefore no catalyst content at all. This is the path-level substitutability Atlas recorded as the reason the link is not a choke point, firing.
The engine tier loses the increment rather than the base, because backup duty and the existing pipeline continue. Medium rather than large for that reason.
Same loss of the marginal campus, cushioned by a backlog already sold out years forward, which means the effect shows up in new orders long before it shows up in revenue.
An exempt project needs far less of this work. The stage's demand is proportional to the number of permits actually being argued, and this scenario reduces that count.
Monitoring conditions attach to permitted combustion sources. Fewer of them means a smaller installed base to monitor for the life of the plant.

The one link this scenario does not damage. Fuel cells still consume pipeline gas, so the lateral, the compression and the firm transport contract are bought either way, which is precisely why Atlas placed this stage as a topological root rather than a consequence of the permit.

leading_indicators.signal: A hyperscaler or neocloud names fuel cells rather than reciprocating engines or turbines as the primary on-site source for a gigawatt-class campus in a nonattainment county.
leading_indicators.check_basis: BE is the only listed name on this link and it has no file under data/market/, so no level can be set for it without inventing a price. Arm after a request data run covers BE.

leading_indicators.signal: Bloom Energy raises 2026 revenue guidance above the $3.9 billion to $4.2 billion range it has published, on data center orders rather than on utility work.
leading_indicators.check_basis: Same missing market file. The guidance range is a cited company figure, not a repo price, and this repo does not arm checks on figures it has not fetched into data/market/.

leading_indicators.signal: Caterpillar falls to 650 or below, under the 800.25 close recorded for 2026-08-28 in data/market/CAT.json and still well above the 415.12 fifty-two-week low, which is what the combustion side losing the marginal campus looks like on the one link name with a price on disk.

invalidation_signs: State minor source permits for reciprocating and turbine fleets keep issuing at or above the Georgia run rate of the last eighteen months while fuel cell backlogs flatten.
A permitting authority rules that large fuel cell installations are not exempt in its jurisdiction, which would remove the product being sold rather than the competition.
Fuel cell delivery slips past the claimed 90-day window on a named campus, which would convert the advantage from structural to marketing.

scenarios.title: The constraint moves from the agency to the factory
scenarios.narrative: The permit gets easier and the machine still does not arrive. Large frame units already face multi-year lead times and constrained manufacturing slots, one supplier's gas power backlog stands at 69 gigawatts of equipment, and per-kilowatt turbine prices are tracked toward 195% above their 2019 level. In this scenario the binding constraint simply relocates: whatever EPA finalises, the long pole becomes the delivery date, not the permit date. Capture migrates upstream to whoever owns a slot and away from everyone who was selling access to the permit. The permitting consultancy loses its claim on the schedule, the developer pays the equipment price and keeps less of the spread, and the rental fleet gets a longer bridge for a different reason than it expected. This is the scenario that most directly attacks the premise of the whole chain, which is that an air permit is the thing worth mapping.

links_moved.why: A queue the buyer cannot jump is the purest form of pricing power on this map, and it is already posted: 15 gigawatts of new orders taking backlog to 69 gigawatts while per-kilowatt prices track toward 195% above 2019.
Constrained manufacturing slots convert into price on every unit. The 1.5 GW restart is evidence the constraint is real enough for a supplier to reopen a platform it had shut in 2022.
The wait moves from permit to delivery and someone still has to power the campus meanwhile. This link is indifferent to which queue causes the delay, which makes it the natural hedge against S1.
Permitting stops being the long pole, so the urgency premium on getting an application through quickly disappears. Small because the work is still legally required on every project.
They buy their equipment from the links above at those links' prices and sell power on contracts signed earlier. Rising equipment cost lands directly on their spread.

Self-generation gets more expensive per megawatt, which raises the cost of the route around the interconnection queue. Small against a capex base above $700 billion, but it is the direction the price acts on.

leading_indicators.signal: A turbine or engine OEM quotes delivery beyond 2030 on new orders, or announces a second capacity expansion because the first one sold out.
leading_indicators.check_basis: The two OEMs that set price in this tier are carried on the shared stage at position 10 and belong to ai-infrastructure, so arming a check on them here would duplicate a bet this map declares once.

leading_indicators.signal: Tetra Tech falls to 30 or below, under the 36.54 close recorded for 2026-08-28 in data/market/TTEK.json and inside its observed 26.18 to 42.61 fifty-two-week range. The permitting consultancy de-rating further while equipment names re-rate is the cleanest paired expression of the constraint moving from the agency to the factory.
AECOM falls to 62 or below, against the 69.17 close recorded for 2026-08-28 in data/market/ACM.json and a 61.04 fifty-two-week low, confirming the consultancy de-rating is the tier and not one name.

invalidation_signs: Named data center projects slip on permit dates rather than on equipment delivery dates in trade coverage, which would put the constraint back at the agency.
The 1.5 GW of restarted engine capacity ships on schedule in the fourth quarter and quoted lead times shorten, which would say the factory constraint is being solved.
Turbine per-kilowatt pricing flattens or reverses, removing the pricing power this scenario assumes migrates upstream.
